transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Alex from Redwood here, along with Priya our SE, Tom from CSM. Um quick roll call?
[00:12] John Patel: Hey John here, CTO at Sequoia. Maria's on from our networking team, Lisa from compliance, Evan from platform.
[00:18] Alex Morgan: Awesome, thanks. High level today's to nail down the POC scope for private networking and data residency. Obviously, you mentioned regulated PHI flows in the invite, so we'll focus on VPC peering/PrivateLink, regions, and egress. Sound good?
[00:30] Lisa Chen: Yep that's right, we need to make sure data never leaves our EU footprint and all keys are customer-managed.
[00:36] Priya Shah: Great, quick question on success criteria — do you have latency or throughput SLOs for the pilot?
[00:42] John Patel: We're targeting sub-200ms median for single-turn prompts at our typical 2k token context with burst to 20 QPS. For embedding workloads it's looser, but throughput matters. Also cost guidance — we need an estimate for Dedicated vs hosted.
[00:58] Alex Morgan: Okay makes sense. For the POC we usually run two benchmark buckets: conversational generation at your 2k context and embedding batch jobs. We'll run them over PrivateLink and VPC peering where possible, measure median/p95 latencies, token/tps, and token cost.
[01:15] Maria Lopez: Quick network note: our infra sits in eu-west-1 and we have strict egress whitelisting. We prefer VPC peering to keep traffic internal, but we also use PrivateLink for controlled endpoints. There may be firewall rules that block ephemeral outbound ranges.
[01:31] Priya Shah: Good to know. For VPC peering we need your CIDR ranges and a route table update on your side; for PrivateLink we'll ask you to create an endpoint and allow our service NLB — sometimes customers prefer PrivateLink because it avoids route overlap.
[01:48] Maria Lopez: Also, we cannot open a broad outbound port range. If Redwood has a set of static IPs or we can do AWS PrivateLink that's preferred.
[01:56] Alex Morgan: Yes, we can provide static egress IPs for Dedicated and for PrivateLink we just need to publish the service name and NLB config. We'll include both options in the security pack.
[02:06] Lisa Chen: On the compliance side we need SOC2, pen test summary, KMS notes, and an audit log retention policy — plus the legal team will need DPA language that enforces EU data residency.
[02:18] Tom Reyes: We'll send the SOC2 and pen test report, and a DPA template. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we'll discuss envelope encryption and HSM integrations.
[02:30] John Patel: Timeline question — how long to run the POC and what are typical deliverables?
[02:34] Alex Morgan: Typical POCs are 4-6 weeks. Week 0 is network setup and security paperwork, week 1 baseline benchmarks and small sample tests, weeks 2-3 run load tests and tune batching/quantization, week 4 evaluate results and decide on Dedicated pilot. We can compress to 3 weeks if we have all network info and access quickly.
[02:53] Evan Brooks: We can prioritize giving you access to a staging VPC and our test data. We'll also provide metadata about request sizes.
[02:59] Priya Shah: For benchmark specifics we recommend: 1) generation test: 5000 samples, median/p95 latencies, KV cache hit rates, average tokens per request; 2) embedding test: 100k vectors batched in 512s to see throughput and GPU utilization; 3) cost-per-token estimates across quantized variants. We'll attach the plan.
[03:19] John Patel: Is it possible to run a baseline on our infra first to simulate network egress? We need to understand added latency from peering vs PrivateLink.
[03:25] Priya Shah: Absolutely, we can run benchmarks both from your VPC via peering and via PrivateLink to compare. The main variance will be NAT/egress hops and firewall inspection. Sometimes PrivateLink avoids NAT and reduces p95.
[03:38] Maria Lopez: If we use peering, routes are simpler but we need to ensure no overlapping CIDR and that we don't leak via internet gateway; we'll need a cross-team change window.
[03:48] Alex Morgan: Noted. We'll provide a checklist of required route table entries and security groups. We'll also provide a small script to validate connectivity and test ports prior to the change window.
[03:59] Lisa Chen: Regarding data residency — everything stored must remain in eu-west-1. Are there any cases where logs or telemetry could be replicated elsewhere?
[04:07] Tom Reyes: By default hosted telemetry is multi-region for observability, but for this POC we can restrict logs and traces to eu-west-1 for the pilot and provide separate log export options. We'll include retention settings in the security doc.
[04:20] John Patel: Encryption keys — we need BYOK with customer-managed KMS, and we need to see key rotation logs.
[04:27] Alex Morgan: We support BYOK for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we can enable customer-managed keys with limited access. We'll include steps and IAM policies you'll need.
[04:36] Evan Brooks: On the model side, do you provide quantized variants? We want to evaluate 8-bit vs 4-bit for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:42] Priya Shah: Yes, we have several quantization profiles. For the POC we'll run the same model under different quantization and compilation kernels and capture latency, token quality (we'll run a small eval set), and GPU utilization.
[04:56] John Patel: For success criteria, thinking out loud: 1) median latency under 200ms for 2k context at 5 QPS sustained; 2) p95 under 500ms; 3) embedding throughput >3000 vectors/sec; 4) no data crossing EU region; 5) security docs approved. Are those reasonable?
[05:18] Priya Shah: That looks good. We'll map each success criteria to measurable benchmarks and an acceptance threshold.
[05:24] Maria Lopez: Network acceptance: connectivity test via our change window, private IP route validation, and confirmation of static egress IPs if peering is not used.
[05:33] Alex Morgan: We'll also provide a runbook for failover — e.g., if peering fails we can fallback to PrivateLink in the POC.
[05:41] Lisa Chen: Any concerns about telemetry that could contain PHI? We need guaranteed redaction or selective telemetry settings.
[05:48] Tom Reyes: We can redact PII from telemetry and provide filtered traces. We'll show the redaction config in the security pack.
[05:56] John Patel: How do you handle model rollouts? If we pin a model and you push a security patch, how are rollouts controlled?
[06:02] Priya Shah: We support pinned model versions and can do canary rollouts. For POC we'll commit to pinned versions unless you want a performance patch. We'll include rollout options and automated rollback in the runbook.
[06:14] Evan Brooks: For cost estimates, we need a sample of QPS, concurrency and monthly token estimates — we'll provide that but can you give a rough delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[06:23] Alex Morgan: Roughly Dedicated lowers unit cost by ~30-50% depending on utilization and batchability. We'll provide a tailored cost model based on the telemetry you send.
[06:32] John Patel: Any special IAM requirements for PrivateLink?
[06:35] Priya Shah: Standard — you'll create an endpoint and allow the Redwood service principal; we provide the exact policy. For peering we only need route and SG rules.
[06:44] Maria Lopez: One more thing — we have egress inspection that performs TLS MITM for outgoing to cloud services. That may break TLS pinning if Redwood uses custom certs.
[06:53] Alex Morgan: We can support cert pinning exceptions or use PrivateLink to avoid interception. We'll document both paths.
[07:01] Lisa Chen: Legal will want the DPA and a commitment on data residency in writing before we move any PHI into the POC.
[07:07] Tom Reyes: We'll provide DPA templates and can add the residency clause for eu-west-1 for the POC.
[07:14] Alex Morgan: Cool. Let's recap next steps, I'll share the security pack with SOC2/pen test and the network checklist; Priya will share benchmarks and AMI/runners; Maria will share CIDRs and egress rules; Lisa will confirm residency wording; Evan will share expected QPS and sample payloads.
[07:35] John Patel: Sounds good. Are we booking the network test now?
[07:39] Maria Lopez: I can do a morning slot the week of 11/9, prefer 11/10.
[07:44] Alex Morgan: I'll propose 11/10 in the follow-up invite.
[07:47] Priya Shah: We'll also include a lightweight test harness so you can run a single-command connectivity and latency check prior to the window.
[07:55] John Patel: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:58] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone, we'll send the pack by Thursday and follow up with the invite.
[08:03] Lisa Chen: Thank you.
[08:05] Meeting ends.
